solicitations.title: Behavioral Health Services
solicitations.description: This solicitation amendment is issued as a combined synopsis and solicitation for commercial services under the authority of 41 U.S.C. § 3305 (Simplified procedures for small business and commercial items) and 41 U.S.C. § 1901 (Simplified acquisition procedures). Solicitation number W912J726QA0020002 amendment is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for Behavior Health Counseling Support ServiceBehavior Health CounselingSupport Services. This procurement is established as a 100% Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) set-aside in accordance with the Small Business Act, specifically 15 U.S.C. § 637(m) (Women-owned small business companion program). Quotations are solicited exclusively from certified WOSB concerns eligible under the WOSB Program (including Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) concerns) in accordance with the statutory standards of 15 U.S.C. § 637(m) and 13 CFR part 127 . Quotes received from non-eligible concerns will not be considered. The Idaho National Guard J9 Service Member and Family Support have a requirement for Behavior HealthCounseling services to Service Members and their immediate family. The team shall be comprised of three(3) full-time Behavior Health Clinicians and one (1) full-time Admin Support position. This requirment has been updated to meet current organizational needs. Response Deadline: August 31, 2026, at 9:00 AM Mountain Daily Time (MDT) Primary NAICS Code: 621112 – Offices of Mental Health Practitioners (except Physicians) Size Standard: $9,000,000.00 Product Service Code (PSC): Q519 – Behavioral and Mental Health Anticipated Period of Performance: 27 Sep 2026 to 26 Sep 2027 for base period, One (1) 12-monthoption periods and one up to 6-months extension (see 52.217-9 and 52.217-8). Primary performance will be conducted at : Joint Force Headquarters, Gowen Field Military Base, Boise, ID 83705 Regional outreach travel to regional Guard offices (including Caldwell, Twin Falls, Pocatello, Idaho Falls, Lewiston, and Post Falls) may be required occasionally. INSTRUCTIONS FOR PROPOSAL SUBMISSION Quotations must be submitted electronically to the Contracting Officer, Natasha Spratt, at natasha.m.spratt2.civ@army.mil no later than August 31, 2026, at 9:00 AM MDT . All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted via email no later than August 17, 2026 . Quote Preparation: Offerors shall prepare their quotations in strict accordance with the requirements, instructions, terms, and conditions contained in this combined synopsis/solicitation, the performance work statement (PWS), and any subsequent formal amendments issued by the Government. Failure to address all requirements or incorporate any subsequent solicitation amendments may result in the quotation being determined non-compliant and excluded from further evaluation. Formatting: To ensure a structured, fair, and efficient evaluation, the offeror’s submission shall be divided into three (3) distinct sections, self-contained Portable Document Format (PDF)s compatible with standard readers. Structure: Section I: Section 1 Quote. Complete SF 1449 or the quoter's vendor commercial quote (no page limit). If providing a commercial quote without the SF 1449, the commercial quote MUST include all elements in W912J726QA0020002 clause 52.212-1 paragraph (a), and the statement requested in (a)(6), provide information pertaining to price only and provide complete pricing per SF 1449 line items schedule excluding CLIN 0005 and 1005 travel. Section II: Section 2 Capability Statement. A capability describing how the quoter intends to provide the services required in this solicitation. Stating "will comply with PWS" is not sufficient. The statement must describe the quoter's capability to meet the agency's needs as described in this solicitation. Not to exceed ten pages , Times New Roman or Arial, size 12, margins at 1-inch, single space. Section III: Section 3 Past Performance. The Government will review information obtained from Government sources including Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS), System of Award Responsibility/Qualifications (also known as Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System (FAPIIS)), Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) Score, and other sources of information. Quoters shall submit a three-page past performance sheet. The past performance attachment can include Federal, non-Federal, and Private Sector. The combined experience submitted to the Government shall not exceed three pages, font Times New Roman or Arial, size 12, margins at 1-inch, single space. Information exceeding three pages will not be considered. Do NOT include Sections 1, 2 and 3 into a single document. Sections shall be submitted as separate documents. Basis of Award: Evaluation factors. The Government will award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) purchase order resulting from this solicitation to the responsible quoter who provides the lowest acceptable quote that demonstrates understanding of the requirements and conformance with the solicitation. This acquisition is being conducted strictly under simplified procedures for commercial products and commercial services. The Government is not conducting a source selection, and procedures from RFO Part 15 do not apply. To efficiently identify the lowest acceptable quote, the Government may evaluate quotes by first ranking them from lowest to highest price. The Government will then evaluate the technical and past performance factors of the lowest-priced quote. If the lowest-priced quote is determined to be acceptable, the Government may evaluate no other quotes and proceed to award. Quotes failing to meet all the terms and conditions of this solicitation, including buy terms, line-item descriptions, and attachments, will not be evaluated for award. The Government reserves the right to seek clarifications on the contents of the quote if determined necessary by the Contracting Officer. Quotes will be evaluated with the following review criteria: (i) Technical: The degree to which the quoter's proposed service meets the Government's requirements. Merely stating 'will comply with all PWS requirements' is insufficient. The Technical Proposal will be evaluated qualitatively and assigned one of the following adjectival ratings: Technical Adjectival Rating Evaluation Definition Outstanding Proposal meets all requirements and demonstrates an exceptional clinical or management approach. Contains multiple strengths that significantly benefit J9 operations, contains no weaknesses, and the risk of unsuccessful performance is extremely low. Good Proposal meets all requirements and demonstrates a thoroughly solid clinical or management approach. Contains at least one or more strengths that benefit J9 operations, contains few minor weaknesses, and the risk of unsuccessful performance is low to moderate. Acceptable Proposal meets all requirements and demonstrates an adequate clinical and management approach. Contains no significant strengths, contains some minor weaknesses, and the risk of unsuccessful performance is moderate. Marginal Proposal fails to meet one or more minor PWS requirements, contains notable weaknesses, and has a high risk of unsuccessful performance. Deficiencies are significant but correctable. Unacceptable Proposal fails to meet major requirements, contains significant deficiencies, represents an unacceptably high risk of performance failure, and cannot be made acceptable without major, complete revisions. (ii) Past Performance: The Government will consider primary Government sources for past performance such as Supplier Performance Risk System, Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS), Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System (FAPIIS), and other sources. Absent past performance with Government, the Government will consider experience from the commercial market and/or experience as a subcontractor. Past performance shall be relevant to the type of work in the Performance Work Statement. The Government will evaluate the recency, relevancy, and quality of the past performance data to assign a Performance Confidence Rating as follows: Past Performance Rating Evaluation Definition Substantial Confidence Based on the offeror’s recent and highly relevant performance record, the Government has a high expectation that the offeror will successfully perform the required clinical and administrative effort. Satisfactory Confidence Based on the offeror’s recent and relevant performance record, the Government has a reasonable expectation that the offeror will successfully perform the required effort. Neutral Confidence No recent or relevant performance record is available, or the performance record is so sparse that no meaningful confidence assessment rating can be reasonably assigned. This rating is treated as "Neutral" and is neither favorable nor unfavorable. Limited Confidence Based on the offeror’s performance record, the Government has a low expectation that the offeror will successfully perform the required effort. No Confidence Based on the offeror’s performance record, significant and extreme performance issues exist, and the Government has no expectation that the offeror will successfully perform the required effort. Price. Price will be evaluated to identify the lowest acceptable quote. The Government will evaluate the quoted price to determine price reasonableness. Price reasonableness will be established by comparing the quoted prices received in response to the solicitation, comparing quotes to the Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE), or using other accepted techniques. Options. The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if the option prices are significantly unbalanced. The evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise the option(s). Notice of award. The purchase order is the Government's offer to a supplier to buy certain products or services upon specified terms and conditions. A binding contract is formed when the supplier accepts the Government's offer, either by written acceptance of the purchase order or substantial performance of the purchase order. The contracting officer may request that the contractor provide written acceptance of the order. Responsibility Determination: The Contracting Officer must determine that the apparent successful quoter is responsible before awarding a purchase order. Separate from the price evaluation described in paragraph (a)(2)(iii), if the lowest acceptable quote features a price that is abnormally low, the Contracting Officer may use that as an indicator of performance risk. In such cases, the Contracting Officer may require the quoter to provide additional information (such as a breakdown of labor rates, material costs, or a risk mitigation plan) specifically to make an affirmative determination of responsibility and ensure the quoter has the capacity and competence to perform the requirement at the quoted price. Failure to demonstrate the capacity to perform at the quoted price may result in a determination of non-responsibility. Because this solicitation is set aside for Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSB), any determination of nonresponsibility for the apparent successful quoter will be referred to the cognizant Small Business Administration (SBA) office for a Certificate of Competency (COC) determination. Note: Quoters are reminded that, a quote is not an offer. All submissions will be treated as QUOTATIONS, regardless of how Quoters decide to label or name their submissions. Quoters are toreview SF 1449 52.212-1, 52.212-2, and Attachment 3 RFI Q&A for additional information. In the event of a discrepancy between this combined solicitation and the SF 1449, the SF 1449 shall govern. Anticipated Date of Award:18 September 2026

solicitations.description: Note to Offerors: This solicitation is currently unfunded. However, should funding become available, some or all of the options MAY BE funded. See 52.232-18 Availability of Funds Clause within attached solicitation. See 52.212-2 for evaluation factors for award within the attached solicitation. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number FA468626Q0019 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for CE MHE Attachments & Trailers . The 9th Civil Engineer Squadron (9 CES) is tasked with maintaining base infrastructure, airfield clear zones, perimeter fence lines, training areas, and wildfire mitigation zones at Beale Air Force Base. Dense vegetation, brush, and small-to-medium trees present ongoing safety, security, and fire hazards. To maintain operational readiness, execute land-clearing missions, and ensure the rapid deployment of excavation assets, 9 CES requires specialized compact excavator attachments and heavy-duty transport trailers. The procurement of these attachments and trailers will directly enhance the squadron's capability to perform rapid vegetative clearing, firebreak maintenance, and tactical asset transport. Please see attached Statement of Need and Solicitation for requirement specifications. DELIVERY IS REQUIRED 45 DAYS ARO. Email all quotes to the Contracting Officer – SSgt Wyatt Lundgreen, wyatt.lundgreen@us.af.mil and Contract Specialist – SrA Cindy Kwan, cindy.kwan@us.af.mil.

solicitations.title: 50mm weapon based Air Defense Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS)
solicitations.description: Description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command - New Jersey, on behalf of the Office of the Project Manager, Maneuver Ammunition Systems (PM-MAS), is seeking to identify potential sources capable of providing a 50mm weapon based Air Defense Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) system. Specifications: Interested parties are requested to outline their existing or conceptual capabilities to integrate a 50mm ammunition solution to effectively track, engage, and defeat Class 1, 2, and 3 UAS threats. To support potential development, integration, and demonstration efforts, the USG may consider providing the following: Hardware (Loan): One (1) XM913 50mm cannon assembly. Ammunition: Required quantities of 50mm ammunition for testing and demonstration. Technical Data: Necessary technical information, specifications, and interfaces required for system integration *. Test Facilities: Access to a USG test facility to conduct a live-fire capability demonstration. Submission Information: THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION AND DOES NOT OBLIGATE THE GOVERNMENT TO ISSUE A SOLICITATION. Please be advised that the Government will not pay for any information submitted under this announcement. Interested companies should submit their qualifications and capabilities electronically within 30 days of this notice to: michael.t.lau3.civ@army.mil and jennifer.m.rustwick.civ@army.mil to the original response date, which is no later than 31 August 2026 @ 3 PM EST. Interested companies should respond by providing the Government with the following information: (1) Name of company and CAGE Code; (2) Point of Contacts name, telephone number and E-mail address; (3) Company address; (4) Business size information; (5) Identification of whether you are interested in this opportunity as a prime or a subcontractor; (6) A detailed description of the company’s capabilities pertaining to C-UAS, proposed C-UAS system architecture, fire control/sensor integration, detailed draft test or demonstration plan, ] and how the platform will successfully employ the 50x228mm ammunition against the specified target set. In addition, the response shall provide a detailed, estimated timeline and schedule to design, integrate, and deliver a weapon system ready for a live-fire demonstration. (7) A brief summary of possible partnering/teaming arrangements; Please identify any proprietary information submitted. A respondent to this survey must have the majority of the skills and facilities that are required to manufacture this item. If a respondent does not have these resources (technical, manufacturing, personnel, etc.) available, then it must demonstrate its ability to obtain them in a reasonable time period. If a respondent chooses to utilize the services of sub-tier vendors or subcontractors, those vendors or subcontractors must also meet the same resource criteria as the prime contractor. Point of Contact & Industry Discussions: To facilitate a comprehensive exchange of information regarding the requirements of this market survey, industry partners may contact the government representatives listed below. Primary Contracting POC: Michael T. Lau, Contract Specialist, michael.t.lau3.civ@army.mil Primary Technical POC: Kahraman Koseoglu, 120mm KE and 50mm Team Lead, kahraman.c.koseoglu.civ@army.mil, (520) 691-1812 The Government encourages interested parties to request a follow-up teleconference to further discuss the technical details and mission requirements. Please coordinate all teleconference requests through both listed points of contact no later than August 24, 2026, at 3:00 PM EST. *Performance Specifications or Technical Data: AT THIS TIME, NO PERFORMANCE SPECIFICATIONS OR TECHNICAL DATA WILL BE PROVIDED. In the event that the United States Government (USG) establishes a formal requirement for the 50mm CUAS system, relevant information will be distributed to support the effort at that time. To expedite future access, the USG invites interested parties to proactively submit a completed AMSTA-AR Form 1350 and an active DD Form 2345 (Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement) now. Completing these security steps ahead of time will ensure the seamless distribution of restricted data if a formal requirement materializes. Please note: Providing these forms at this stage is strictly optional. Submissions without an accompanying AMSTA-AR Form 1350 or DD Form 2345 are fully acceptable and will not disqualify a company's response to this market survey. In the event the Government releases technical data with Limited Distribution Technical Data (only if this action materializes into a formal requirement) (i.e. anything other than Distribution A), Requests for the performance specification shall be submitted in writing using AMSTA-AR Form 1350 Technical Data Request Questionnaire (attached) along with a signed DD 2345 Military Critical Technical Data Agreement form (attached). Offerors must be registered with the U.S./Canada Joint Certification Office to obtain a copy of the limited distribution data (See https://www.public.dacs.dla.mil/jcp/ext/ for instructions and information). Offerors should submit their certification via DD Form 2345 or register immediately. In order to provide the data to foreign subcontractors, offerors must apply for an export license. An offeror's delay in applying for DD 2345 certification or an export license will not be a basis to extend the closing date of any future request for proposal. If your company does not have a signed DD 2345 Military Critical Technical Data Agreement Form, then before submitting your company’s JCP Certification Request or DLA Enhanced Validation Request to JCP directly, please make sure the following items have been completed: 1. Complete SAM registration and ensure that all your CAGE information is correct and active at https://sam.gov/content/home. 2. Your NIST assessment results must be documented in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) at https://www.sprs.csd.disa.mil/. 3. Review and complete the Introduction to Proper Handling of DoD Export- Controlled Technical Data. a. Export Control Compliance Training for all Data Custodians and Alternate Data Custodians who require access to DoD Unclassified Export Controlled Technical Data. Please review and complete Page 15 of the attached Introduction to Proper Handling of DoD Export-Controlled Technical Data Training Course. Once completed, print Page 15, “Certification Statement of Export Control Compliance,” and attach the certificate to your JCP Application. 4. Provide all information required for "What do you do" (Block 4, Business Activities, of the DD2345 certificate). See the help symbol "?" for instructions. Keep your statements brief as space is limited. If all required information is not provided, your incomplete application will be returned in the JCP Portal. If you have any questions or concerns related to your DD2345 submission, please do not hesitate to email JCP-ADMIN@DLA.MIL This is a market survey, not a pre-solicitation notice. If a formal solicitation is generated at a later date a solicitation notice will be published. All information is to be submitted at no cost or obligation to the Government. Questions and Answers Q. Are you seeking a complete weapon system or only specific subsystems? A. We are providing the XM913 weapon system. Any additional components need for UAS defeat is on the vendor to provide. Q. Do you require HEP or Next-Generation (guided) technology? A. No requirements on technology just need solution to achieve UAS defeat. Q. Is there a defined page limit for the submission? A. No page limit Q. What is the anticipated range of quantities for ammunition deliveries? A. TBD at this time Q. Will the USG Technical Data Package (TDP) be provided for development? Warhead A. No Fuze A. Only communication protocol Propellant A. No A. Interface Capability Documents (ICDs) will be provided and actual Target Practice w/ Tracer ammunition will be provided for testing set up. Additional requests can be submitted and shall be considered. Please provide in response what specific data would be requested. Q. What platform will the system be fired from? A. No platform requirement is defined. Q. For the current opportunity, are you evaluating fire control and targeting technologies? A. We are evaluating the system level capability for a 50mm CUAS solution. If their capabilities (existing or conceptual) can be integrated with the XM913 we will evaluate per the posting.
